name: IRR (Single Cash Flow)
description: Calculate the annualized rate of return for a single future cash flow relative to an initial investment. This is the simplified single-cash-flow case-interview shortcut, not full multi-period IRR with multiple cash flows.
formula: IRR (single cash flow) = (Future Value / Initial Investment)^(1/Years) − 1
business_contexts: an investor estimating the annualized return on a single exit payout
a private equity firm estimating the annualized return on a hold-to-sale investment
a startup investor estimating the annualized return on a single funding round
a real estate investor estimating the annualized return on a property sale
a venture fund estimating the annualized return on a single portfolio exit
question_patterns: Given the initial investment, future value, and years below, what is the IRR?
Calculate the annualized IRR from the figures given, assuming a single cash flow at exit.
What annualized return does this single cash flow investment generate, given the figures below?
Calculate IRR for a single future payout using the figures shown.
Using the figures below, what is the annualized IRR for this single cash flow?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate the value multiple = future_value / initial_investment
key_insight: This is the single-cash-flow case-interview shortcut for IRR, not full multi-period IRR — real IRR with multiple interim cash flows requires iterative solving, which is out of scope for a closed-form drill.
common_mistakes: Applying the exponent to the difference (future value minus initial investment) instead of to the ratio between them
Forgetting to take the years-th root, and instead dividing the multiple by years
framework_soundbite: Single-cash-flow IRR is the growth multiple raised to the power of 1 over years, minus 1 — annualizing a single payout, not solving a full cash flow schedule.
